This Miscellaneous First Appeal Coming On For
Admission This Day, K.S.Mudagal J., Delivered The
Following:
 Judgment
"Whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal to the appellants in MVC No.133/2016 by the Principal District Judge and M.A.C.T, Chikkamagaluru is just"? is the question involved in this case.
2. The appellants are the parents and younger brother of deceased Nagananda.

On 19.06.2015 at 5.00 p.m. when Nagananda was traveling as pillion rider with one Suhaksha on motorbike bearing registration No.K.A.18/K.6322 near the house of one Ganesh Hegde in Neralakodige on Sringeri-Agumbe road, light goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA.19/B.0073 hit the said motorbike.
Due to the injuries suffered in the accident, both rider and pillion rider of the motorbike died.

sentences.text: 3. The dependents of motorcycle rider Suhaksha filed MVC No.33/2016 and the appellants filed MVC No.133/2016 before the Principal District Judge and MACT, Chikkamagaluru against the respondents claiming that accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the goods vehicle bearing No.KA.19/B.0073 and consequent death of Suhaksha and Nagananda they have suffered damages.
The appellants claimed the compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents.
4. The Tribunal consolidated MVC Nos.33/2016 and 133/2016 and recorded the common evidence.

The Tribunal on hearing the parties, partly allowed both the petitions awarding compensation of Rs.7,47,000/- to the claimants in MVC No.33/2016 and Rs.7,83,000/- to the present appellants who are the claimants in MVC No.133/2016.
Challenging the adequacy of compensation awarded to them, the appellants have preferred the above appeal.
5. Similarly, claimants in MVC No.33/2016 preferred MFA No.3574/2018(MV) before this Court.
Admittedly, MFA No.3574/2018(MV) was partly allowed by this court on 09.02.2021.
The copy of the said order is placed by the learned Counsel for the appellant on record.
Under the circumstances, the only question is regarding the adequacy of compensation awarded to the appellants.
6. At the time of accident, the deceased was aged 21 years.
Though the appellants claimed that he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month, there was no proof of such income.
Therefore, his income has to be considered notionally.
The Tribunal has considered his income at Rs.6,000/- per month.
The accident occurred on 19.06.2015.
Considering the age of the deceased and cost of living during that period and wage rates prevailing during that period, the Tribunal should have considered at Rs.9,000/- per month.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi1, and having regard to the age of the deceased, 40% of the income has to be superadded to the income by way of future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.12,600/-.

7. Since the deceased was a bachelor, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation & anr.2, half of the income has to be deducted for his personal expenses.

entities.text: Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation & anr.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, his income comes to Rs.6,300/- per month.
The applicable multiplier is 18.

Hence, the compensation payable on the heads of loss of dependency comes to Rs.13,60,800/-
(Rs.6,300 x 12x 18).
8.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case, each of the appellants are entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- on the head of consortium with an escalation at the rate of 10%.

Therefore AIR 2017 SC 5157 AIR 2009 SC 3104 the compensation payable on the head of consortium which comes to Rs.1,76,000/-(44,000x4).
9.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case referred to supra, the claimants are entitled to compensation on the heads of funeral expenses, loss of estate, which comes to Rs.33,000/-.

Therefore just compensation is as follows:

Conventional heads namely, 33,000/-

The order of the Tribunal needs to be modified accordingly.

Therefore the following:
ORDER
The appeal is partly allowed.

The impugned award is modified as follows:
(i) The appellants/claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,69,800/- with interest thereon at 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
(ii) Respondent No.3 shall deposit the said amount before the Tribunal (on adjusting compensation already deposited if any) within six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this award.
(iii) The order of the Tribunal with regard to apportionment and investment is maintained.
